title: Simultaneous embedding with fixed edges for two graphs
formal: Is there a deterministic algorithm that, given any two finite simple planar graphs \(G_{1}=(V,E_{1})\) and \(G_{2}=(V,E_{2})\) on the same labeled vertex set, decides in polynomial time whether they admit planar topological drawings that coincide on every shared vertex and every shared edge?
why: A central simultaneous graph-drawing problem about making overlapping structures geometrically consistent.

progress.text: The updated survey separates SEFE from geometric and freely redrawn-edge variants.
Two current primary papers describe connected-common-graph SEFE as polynomially solvable and the unrestricted two-graph case as open.
Work on two paths addresses geometric grid optimization, a separate target.

definitions: The input gives \(n\ge 0, V=\{1,\ldots ,n\}\), and two symmetric zero-diagonal \(n\times n\) binary adjacency matrices, with total bit length N; each graph is promised planar. No drawing, vertex coordinates or embedding is supplied. The common graph is \(H=(V,E_{1}\cap E_{2})\), which may be disconnected and have isolated vertices. A drawing assigns distinct points \(p(v)\in \mathbb{R} ^{2}\) to vertices and to each edge uv a simple continuous arc with endpoints \(p(u),p(v)\), whose interior contains no vertex point. Planarity means that arcs for distinct edges of the same graph meet only at a common endpoint, if there is one. A simultaneous drawing uses the same \(p(v)\) in both graphs and exactly the same arc image for every edge in \(E_{1}\cap E_{2}\). Edges exclusive to different graphs may cross each other. Arcs may bend freely; no grid, edge-length, area or bend bound is imposed. The requested output is only YES or NO. Polynomial time means one always-correct deterministic Turing machine and constants \(C,c\ge 1\) with at most \(C(N+1)^{c}\) bit steps on every promised input, with no oracle or advice. “Fixed edges” means shared drawings agree on their common edges, not that any geometry is fixed in the input.
answer_criterion: Prove that a polynomial-time decider exists for all promised pairs, or prove that none exists. A positive answer must cover arbitrary disconnected common graphs and freely chosen embeddings. A nonembeddable pair is a NO instance, not a refutation of polynomial decidability. Hardness for three input graphs, straight-line drawings or an additional optimization objective does not answer this question.

context_blocks.title: Two compatible views of the same objects
context_blocks.text: Think of two network diagrams whose vertices denote the same objects and whose edges describe two relations. Each view must be crossing-free on its own. Shared edges must stay in place when switching views. This is why drawing each graph independently can fail to meet the simultaneous requirement.

context_blocks.title: The union need not be planar
context_blocks.text: Take \(G_{1}\) to be \(K_{5}\) with one edge deleted and \(G_{2}\) to contain just that missing edge on the same five vertices. \(G_{1}\) is planar, and \(G_{2}\) can use the same vertex positions with its edge crossing edges exclusive to \(G_{1}\). This is a valid simultaneous drawing, even though the union is the nonplanar graph \(K_{5}\). Testing the union’s planarity would therefore reject valid instances.

context_blocks.title: The connected common case is solved
context_blocks.text: The checked 2025 papers report polynomial-time algorithms when H is connected. This is connectivity of the shared edges and vertices, not merely connectivity of each input graph. Allowing H to have multiple components introduces compatibility of their positions as well as choices of embeddings, and the unrestricted two-graph question remains open in those sources.

context_blocks.title: Which nearby results apply
context_blocks.text: Three-graph SEFE is NP-complete, but the number two is essential here. The March 2026 work on two paths studies straight-line grid drawings and optimizes geometric quantities. Its hardness result for edge length does not imply hardness of deciding whether unrestricted curved-edge drawings exist.

sentences: Two planar graphs share labeled vertices and possibly some edges.
The question asks whether the existence of compatible planar drawings can be decided in polynomial time.
Each shared vertex and edge must look identical in both drawings, while edges exclusive to different graphs may cross.
The case with connected common graph is known to be efficiently solvable.
The remaining target covers arbitrary common graphs and is distinct from straight-line or three-graph variants.
